data.title: White Wagtail Spotted in Imam Turki bin Abdullah Royal Nature Reserve
data.content:
Rafha, November 22, 2026, SPA -- The Imam Turki bin Abdullah Royal Nature Reserve has documented the presence of the White Wagtail (Motacilla alba) along the edges of rainwater pools within the reserve, highlighting the diversity of its natural habitats and wildlife.
    The bird is among the migratory species that arrive in the Kingdom during autumn and winter as temperatures drop, before returning to their breeding grounds in Europe and Asia with the onset of spring in March and April. It is a common winter visitor to the Kingdom, including Northern Borders Region.
    The White Wagtail is distinguished by its white, black, and gray plumage, with a predominantly gray back, white underparts, and distinctive black markings on its head and chest. The intensity of these markings varies according to the season and the bird's age, making it easily identifiable in open environments.
    Within the reserve, the bird can be seen along the edges of water pools and among surrounding vegetation. Formed by recent rainfall, these temporary pools provide important habitats for wildlife, bringing together water, vegetation, and birdlife. The sighting highlights the ecological importance of seasonal water bodies in attracting wildlife and enriching the reserve's natural environment. It also underscores the need to protect natural habitats, preserve biodiversity, and ensure its sustainability.
    -- SPA
